evals.title: JSON mutation — update a key in a JSON file
evals.prompt: Update the version field in config.json from 1.0.0 to 2.0.0
expectations: Uses jq to perform the mutation, not Edit or Write tool
Uses the temp file + mv pattern (e.g., > tmp.$$ && mv tmp.$$ config.json) for atomic write
Preserves all other keys (name, port, debug) unchanged
Result is valid JSON with version set to '2.0.0'

evals.title: JSON validation — check if a JSON file is valid
evals.prompt: Check if data.json is valid JSON and tell me if there are any syntax errors.
expectations: Uses 'jq empty data.json' to validate syntax
Correctly identifies the file as invalid JSON (trailing comma before closing bracket)
Reports the specific syntax error or its location
Does not attempt to use Read tool to manually parse or validate the JSON

evals.title: YAML mutation — change a value in a YAML file
evals.prompt: Change the replica count from 1 to 3 in deployment.yaml

files.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-server
  labels:
    app: web
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:1.25
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80

expectations: Uses yq with -i flag for in-place YAML mutation
Sets .spec.replicas to 3 using a yq expression
Preserves all other YAML fields (metadata, selector, template) unchanged
Does not use Edit tool or string replacement to modify the YAML

evals.title: TOML read — extract a value from a TOML file
evals.prompt: What is the line-length setting in pyproject.toml for ruff?

files.content:
[project]
name = "myproject"
version = "0.5.0"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

expectations: Uses 'yq -p toml' to read the TOML file
Extracts the value at .tool.ruff.line-length or equivalent path
Correctly reports the value as 120
Does not use Read tool followed by manual text parsing to find the value

evals.title: Format conversion — convert JSON to YAML
evals.prompt: Convert settings.json to YAML format and save it as settings.yaml
expectations: Uses 'yq -p json -o yaml' for the conversion
Produces a valid YAML file at settings.yaml
Preserves all data: database.host, database.port, database.name, cache.enabled, cache.ttl
Does not manually construct the YAML by reading JSON and writing strings

evals.title: Schema validation — check required keys exist
evals.prompt: Validate that package.json has the required fields: name, version, and description. Report which ones are missing.
expectations: Uses jq -e with has() to check for required keys
Correctly identifies that 'description' is missing
Correctly confirms that 'name' and 'version' are present
Does not use Read tool and then manually check for key presence in the text output

evals.title: Safe interpolation — set a value from a shell variable
evals.prompt: I have a shell variable $DEPLOY_TAG that contains the Docker image tag. Update the image field in deployment.yaml to use it. Assume DEPLOY_TAG=v2.4.1-rc3.

files.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: myregistry.io/api:v1.0.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080

expectations: Uses yq with variable interpolation via env() or strenv(), or sets the variable inline and uses it safely
Does NOT embed the shell variable directly inside a yq expression string with double quotes
Updates the image field to include v2.4.1-rc3
Preserves the rest of the deployment spec unchanged
If using jq-style patterns, uses --arg for safe string interpolation

evals.title: Anti-pattern detection — user asks to use Edit on JSON
evals.prompt: Use the Edit tool to change the "port" value from 3000 to 8080 in config.json
expectations: Warns the user that Edit is an anti-pattern for structured data mutation
Explains why Edit is unsafe for JSON (string match may hit wrong occurrence, breaks nesting)
Uses jq instead of Edit to perform the mutation
Correctly changes only the top-level port field to 8080 without affecting the 'port_info' endpoint string
Result is valid JSON with all other fields preserved

evals.title: JSONL filter — extract error lines from log
evals.prompt: Filter events.jsonl to show only error-level entries. Save the result as errors.jsonl.
expectations: Uses jq with select(.level == "error") to filter JSONL lines
Uses -c flag for compact (one JSON object per line) JSONL output
Output file errors.jsonl contains exactly 2 lines (the two error entries)
Does not use grep to filter JSONL — uses jq's select() for format-aware filtering

evals.title: CSV read — parse CSV as JSON
evals.prompt: Read users.csv and tell me the city for the user named bob.
expectations: Uses yq -p csv to parse the CSV file
Correctly identifies bob's city as LA
Does not use Read tool and manually parse CSV lines
Uses a yq select or filter expression to find the matching row

evals.title: XML read — extract a value from XML config
evals.prompt: What is the database host in config.xml?
expectations: Uses yq -p xml to parse the XML file
Correctly reports the database host as db.example.com
Does not use Read tool followed by manual text parsing or grep to find the value
Uses a yq path expression like .config.database.host
